Kareli Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kareli, Georgia

Not demolished. Kareli, first recorded as a village in 1715 and granted town status in 1981, has a Jewish history dating back centuries, though detailed records are scarce before the 19th century; one historian traces Jewish migration there from Zovreti as early as the 16th century. About 400 Jews lived in Kareli by the early 20th century, supporting a synagogue and rabbi. Two synagogues existed historically - one built in the 19th century and rebuilt in 1990 after a fire (no longer active), and a second built in 1902 by Rabbi Abram Tsitsuashvili, later damaged in a 1940 earthquake and rebuilt as a matzah bakery. Twentieth-century emigration to Gori, Tbilisi, and eventually Israel led to the community's near-total disappearance. The cemetery dates to the 19th century and remained active until the second half of the 20th century, just before the main wave of Aliyah; most burials date to the 1970s, with the earliest legible tombstone from 1906 and the most recent from 1998.
